one_liner: Senior Executive Service leader running the U.S. Mint's coin and collectibles (numismatic) sales, marketing, revenue and customer strategy, managing managers in Washington, DC.
fit_summary: This is an SES role requiring proven executive-level leadership of sales, marketing and business development for a large, geographically dispersed organization, led through subordinate managers (TQ 1 and TQ 2). Nothing on file shows Daniel has executive sales/marketing or multi-layer supervisory experience; the IEM consulting background and policy knowledge help mainly with ECQ 1. Unless Daniel has led a large sales or marketing organization, this application is unlikely to pass the minimum-qualifications screen.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include public, SES, competitive and excepted); must be a U.S. citizen or U.S. national.
Your resume (2 pages maximum) must show all five ECQs and both TQs; there is no separate narrative, and pages beyond 2 are not reviewed or may be disqualified.
TQ 1 requires executive-level experience leading sales, marketing and business development through subordinate managers for a large, complex, geographically dispersed organization.

If you are selected for a first career SES appointment, you will need OPM QRB certification, which includes an ECQ-based structured interview. You will also face a one-year probationary period, a background investigation, and an annual OGE-278e financial disclosure.
strategy: Before investing time, honestly check whether you have led sales, marketing or business development at an executive level through other managers. If not, skip this posting and target GS-11/12/13 program, outreach, or legislative/intergovernmental affairs roles at FEMA, DHS, Treasury, or Virginia agencies.

If you have relevant experience from IEM, frame any business development, capture/proposal, or client-growth work with government clients as sales and partnership work. Quantify contract value, revenue, team size, and the number of managers you led, all of which must be accurate.
Use ECQ 1 to show your knowledge of the American system of government and public policy, ideally tied to concrete work serving public-sector clients.
Fit all five ECQs and both TQs into two pages using compact Challenge-Context-Action-Result style bullets. For each job, list dates, hours per week, supervisory span, and budget size.
Apply between October 20 and November 3, 2026, and upload the resume as a PDF, confirming the 2-page limit before you submit.
resume_bullets: Led [business development/capture] for [type of government emergency-management contracts] at IEM, winning [number] awards worth [$ value] by building relationships with [client agencies].
Directed a team of [number] staff including [number] managers across [locations] to deliver [program/service], meeting [performance goal] within a [$ budget].
Identified [market/client trend] and developed a [partnership/outreach strategy] that increased [customer engagement metric] by [verified %].
interview_questions: Describe a time you set strategic direction for a sales or marketing organization and led through subordinate managers to hit revenue targets.
How have you cut wasteful spending or improved efficiency through process or technology changes?
Tell us about holding a manager accountable for poor performance while leading the organization through change.
How would you expand customer engagement for a government product line like the Mint's numismatic portfolio?
watch_outs: The executive sales and marketing TQs are likely unmet by your known background, so this is a major disqualification risk.
The role has no telework, and the daily commute from Manassas to DC is long.
The closing window is short (October 20 to November 3, 2026), and the 2-page resume limit is strictly enforced.
SES appointment brings a probationary period, QRB certification, and public financial disclosure requirements.
